physicalNotes: Radius 24 +/- 15 solar radii from Comerón et al. (2003), A&A 400, 137, section 3.1: L = 2.6 x 10^4 L_sun (Delta log L = 0.4, at the paper's distance of NGC 253, 2.6 Mpc) and T_eff = 15,000 K (about +/- 3,000 K), through L = 4 pi R^2 sigma T^4 with the nominal solar 5772 K (IAU 2015 Resolution B3, Prsa et al. 2016, arXiv:1605.09788); the paper prints no radius, and no measurement of this star's size exists (https://doi.org/10.1051/0004-6361:20021909): 16,696,800 km at 695,700 km per solar radius. Mass 12 solar masses from Comerón et al. (2003), A&A 400, 137, abstract and section 3.1: a mass of 12 M_sun, the initial mass that the evolutionary models of Meynet & Maeder (2000) give at its temperature and luminosity; not a dynamical measurement (https://doi.org/10.1051/0004-6361:20021909); GM is that mass times the JPL solar GM. Temperature 15000 +/- 3000 K from Comerón et al. (2003), A&A 400, 137, section 3.1: T_eff = 15,000 K, uncertain by about 3,000 K, from its B-V colour through the colour, temperature and bolometric correction relations of Castelli (1999) (https://doi.org/10.1051/0004-6361:20021909). presentationUp: the display axis is a sky-plane convention; the spin axis's position angle on the sky is not measured.

sources.distance: At NGC 253's own distance, 7,351 pc from its centre on the sky: the star is in the galaxy's halo, its sight line does not cross the disc there, and its depth along that line is not measured (Comerón et al. (2003), A&A 400, 137 also take the galaxy's distance for it). The galaxy's distance: RadburnSmith2011ApJS..195...18R: The GHOSTS Survey. I. Hubble Space Telescope Advanced Camera for Surveys Data (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2011ApJS..195...18R); catalogue reference RadburnSmith2011ApJS..195...18R: 3467368.50453 pc (-109992.362096/+113595.866501); trgb (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2011ApJS..195...18R): 3467369 pc; Gaia DR3 cannot see the star
sources.properMotion: 10.1051/0004-6361:20030311 row Object = J004805.3-251745, RA = 00:48:05.3, Dec = -25:17:45 measures no proper motion; zero is assumed (at 3,467,369 pc, 1 mas/yr would be 16,437 km/s across the sky)
sources.radialVelocity: Comerón et al. (2003), A&A 400, 137, section 3: v = 279 +/- 15 km/s from its Balmer and Ca II K lines, against the galaxy's 251 km/s (https://doi.org/10.1051/0004-6361:20021909)
